title: Proof-of-Control Evidence Token (JWT/JSON rendering)
description: The claim set of a Proof-of-Control Evidence token, rendered as JSON for a JWT-based deployment. Structurally equivalent to the CWT/CBOR rendering in poc-evidence.cddl. Digests are OCI-style tagged strings 'alg:hex' so that a hash-algorithm migration does not require new claims.

iss.description: Issuer: the attesting environment or issuing service.

iat.description: Issuance time, seconds since the Unix epoch.

nonce.description: Relying-party challenge. Binds the token to one request and defeats replay (C7.1.4).

eat_profile.description: EAT profile identifier. A verifier that does not recognise this value MUST NOT interpret the poc_claims object.

signature.description: Detached signature over the canonical form of this object with the 'signature' member removed. See canonicalization.md.

hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal. Uppercase is a canonicalization error, not a stylistic one.

digest.description: Algorithm-tagged digest, e.g. 'sha-256:9f86d0...'. The tag is mandatory so that evidence produced before a hash migration remains interpretable after it (C6.3.4). Each algorithm carries its own length: an earlier pattern accepted any tag with any length in 64-128 hex, so 'sha-384:' followed by a 32-byte digest validated. A digest whose declared algorithm does not match its width is not a stylistic error -- it is a value that cannot be what it says it is.

agent_id.description: Stable identifier for the agent instance (C5.1.1). A DID is RECOMMENDED.

initiating_user.description: The principal on whose authority the agent acts (C5.1.2). Delegation chains are represented by a chain of tokens, not by a list here.

agbom_digest.description: Digest of the agent bill of materials in force for this step (C1.2).

interception_point.description: Which of the eight lifecycle hooks of C7.1 produced this record.

step_index.description: Monotonic per agent, starting at 0, with no gaps. A gap is an omission (C7.3.1).

chain_head.description: H(previous_head || canonical_snapshot_hash || verdict). Sequential integrity for a verifier replaying the whole history.

merkle_root.description: RFC 6962 tree head over all leaves through this step. This is what an inclusion proof reconstructs (C7.3.4).

tree_size.description: Number of leaves the merkle_root covers. An inclusion proof is meaningless without it.

policy_bundle_hash.description: Digest of the exact policy that produced the verdict (C4.2). Without it a verdict cannot be re-derived.

canonical_snapshot_hash.description: Digest of the canonical snapshot the policy actually evaluated. The relying party recomputes this from the request it is asked to perform; a mismatch means the executed action is not the evidenced one (Theorem 1).

path_summary_hash.description: Digest of the bounded path summary at evaluation time (C4.1.7).

dispatched_snapshot_hash.description: Digest of the action actually dispatched when verdict is MODIFY. Required in that case: validate.py rejects a MODIFY token without it (modify-unbound).

verdict.description: The binding decision. MODIFY means the dispatched action differs from the proposed one and MUST itself be evidenced.

reason.description: Human-readable rationale. Advisory: a verifier MUST NOT rely on it for any security decision.

alg.description: Signature algorithm, named in every record so that a migration does not orphan published evidence (C6.3.4).

platform.description: SOFTWARE means no hardware isolation. Such evidence cannot support a Tier 3 or Tier 4 claim, and a verifier MUST refuse to treat it as if it could.

measurement.description: Measurement of the evaluated code identity, compared against a published reference value (C8.1.7).
